description:
Non-required nits surfaced during code review of the six explorer-*
TODOs completed 2026-04-17 (ultraplan phases A-F):

  - explorer-result-detail-median-first        (Phase A)
  - explorer-master-leaderboard-home           (Phase B)
  - explorer-query-workbench                   (Phase C)
  - explorer-unified-chart-panel               (Phase D)
  - explorer-url-synced-filter-state           (Phase E)
  - explorer-pipeline-meta-leaderboard-widening (Phase F)

All typecheck and Vitest tests are green; post-feature fix commits
(59aa46440, a79af024c) already addressed required issues. These are
cleanup items only.

preserves.behavior: All existing Vitest suites continue to pass (229 tests across 23 files as of 2026-04-18)
Python explorer_pipeline tests continue to pass
meta_leaderboard.json artifact shape remains backward-compatible for any frontend older than w5

verifications.command: cd results-explorer && npm run typecheck && npm test

work_units.notes:
Home.tsx line 98 rounds avg_rank to 2 decimals; MetaLeaderboard.tsx
line 218 renders via `.toFixed(1)`. Pick one (1 decimal is enough
for visual scan) and drop the more precise round at the source.
work_units.summary: Align avg_rank decimal precision across Home.tsx and MetaLeaderboard.tsx

work_units.notes:
ResultDetail.tsx uses <th onClick={toggleSort(...)}> without
role="button", tabIndex, or onKeyDown. Add keyboard affordances
matching the MetaLeaderboard a11y pattern: role="button",
tabIndex=0, Enter/Space activation.
work_units.summary: Keyboard-enable sortable table headers in ResultDetail.tsx

work_units.notes:
`sortedMedians` / `sortedRawQueries` (lines 68-86) sort on every
render. Low impact but easy useMemo win.

ResultDetail.tsx:282 and BenchmarkIndex/Compare/PlatformIndex
pass `context={{ kind: "...", ... }}` as inline literals. Each
render produces a new object identity, invalidating the
applicableCharts/summary/historical/compareRows useMemos inside
ChartPanel. Wrap each site's context in useMemo or let
ChartPanel accept discrete props (kind, detail, summary, ...)
and build the discriminated union internally.
work_units.summary: Memoize ChartPanel context objects at call sites

work_units.notes:
chartRegistry.parity.test.ts regex-matches _CHART_SPECS in
chart_types.py. Any Python syntax change (formatting, comments
inside the tuple) risks silently breaking the extraction.
Generate `tests/parity/fixtures/chart_ids.json` from Python
during make parity-fixtures and have the test read that file
instead. Related to follow-up nit w11 on
explorer-visualization-review-followup-nits.
work_units.summary: Emit chart spec IDs as a JSON fixture for the parity test

work_units.notes:
ChartPanel.tsx:419 hardcodes `benchmark === "tpch" || benchmark === "tpcds"`
as the Power@Size carve-out when summary.ranking is missing. The
ranking config emitted by the pipeline should always be present
- if it isn't, error/log rather than guess. Alternatively read
a shared RANKING_METRIC_BY_FAMILY mirror on the frontend.

Call sites like Home.tsx:23-24 pass fresh `[]` as `initial`. The
popstate useEffect at useUrlState.ts:116 depends on `initial`,
so it re-subscribes on every render. Behavior is correct
(cleanup runs) but wasteful. Either hoist the empty-array
literals to module-level constants or ignore `initial` in the
effect dep array (it is semantically a constant after mount).
work_units.summary: Stabilize useUrlState's initial/value references at call sites

work_units.notes:
useUrlState.ts:126 returns a new setValue function each render.
Downstream memoized subtrees re-render when it is passed as a
prop. useCallback((v) => ..., [key, initial]) is a minor but
easy win.

Home.tsx buildCohortHref (lines 161-168) only carries `tuning` to
the cohort landing page. Passing `trust` and `window` (date) as
well would keep the filter slice consistent when navigating to a
cohort detail - verify BenchmarkIndex reads the same param names.
work_units.summary: Preserve trust and date-window filters in MetaLeaderboard cohort hrefs

work_units.notes:
MetaLeaderboard.tsx line 304 falls back to `${rank.rank}/${rank.total}`
when renderCellValue returns JSX ("ranks" mode). Factor the a11y
announcement text out of renderCellValue so describeCell doesn't
mirror the formatting logic.
work_units.summary: Clean up describeCell's JSX-vs-string coupling in MetaLeaderboard.tsx

work_units.notes:
pipeline.py _build_meta_leaderboard (line 242) uses
`len(sorted_rows)` for `total`, which counts platforms whose
primary metric is None. A cohort of 3 where 1 platform has no
metric currently shows "1/3" and "2/3" - arguably it should be
"1/2" and "2/2". Consider `sum(1 for r in sorted_rows if _get_val(r) is not None)`.
work_units.summary: Clarify MetaRank `total` - count only rankable rows, not null-metric rows

work_units.notes:
pipeline.py:240-247 duplicates primary_metric/primary_order into
every rank cell when it's already on the parent cohort record.
Frontend reads cohort.primary_order anyway - we can trim the
per-cell copies to keep meta_leaderboard.json smaller and remove
the divergence risk. Requires follow-up on frontend: drop the
optional fields from MetaRank and update MetaLeaderboard.tsx
cellShadeMetric to pull from the cohort.
work_units.summary: Drop duplicated primary_metric/primary_order from per-cell MetaRank

work_units.notes:
Query.tsx:285-295 hardcodes `{count: 0}` for each date-window
option. Add a dedicated facet query that buckets rows by
(now − 30d, 90d, 365d) so users see the impact before clicking.
work_units.summary: Populate Query workbench date-window facet counts

work_units.notes:
Query.tsx:192 uses
  COPY (...) TO '${exportName}' (FORMAT CSV, ...)
exportName is currently built from Date.now() so injection is
impossible today, but any future change that weaves user input
into the filename would silently become injectable. Either
runtime-assert `exportName` matches `/^benchbox-query-export-\d+\.csv$/`
or use DuckDB parameterization if the driver supports it.
work_units.summary: Defensively sanitize or parameterize exportName in CSV COPY TO

work_units.notes:
Query.tsx:399 uses `Object.keys(sqlRows[0]!)` to derive headers.
Heterogeneous rows (UNION ALL over schema-drifted views) would
miss columns only present in later rows. Compute the union of
keys across all rows, or warn the user.
work_units.summary: Stabilize Advanced SQL result column derivation

work_units.notes: Query.tsx line 232 uses literal backticks in prose - they render as visible characters rather than code styling. Replace with `results.duckdb` spans.
work_units.summary: Render code-marker backticks as inline <code> in Query.tsx copy
